items.title: Geometric normality at a point is unchanged by an arbitrary extension of the base field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For X over k, a field extension k'/k, a point x and a point x' of X_{k'} above it, the lemma shows that geometric normality at x is equivalent to geometric normality at x' over k', with the global statement as a corollary (statement lines 2209-2222). The forward implication is formal. For the converse the author again reduces to the defining condition on finite purely inseparable extensions: given k''/k finite purely inseparable and a point x'' above x, one chooses a common extension field of k' and k'' with a point above both, and observes that the map between the corresponding local rings is a flat local homomorphism, hence faithfully flat; normality upstairs therefore descends to the local ring over k'', and the pointwise criterion gives geometric normality over k (proof lines 2225-2240). The claim is H2: the same reduction pattern as for geometric regularity, with descent of normality along faithfully flat local maps in place of descent of regularity.
